page: OVHcloud a100-720 is a high-density GPU-accelerated cloud instance within the Cloud GPU family, provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is built on x86_64 architecture and provides 60 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz. System memory is sized at 720 GB, providing an allocation of 12.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is delivered by four NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs, totaling 320 GB of VRAM with 80 GB dedicated to each accelerator.

Local ephemeral storage is provided via a 500 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. Given the compute density and large memory footprint, the 500 GB local storage pool is modest, meaning datasets exceeding this threshold will depend on external block or object storage. The configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires consideration during network design.

By bundling four 80 GB A100 GPUs with 720 GB of system memory, the instance delivers high compute efficiency for workloads that fit primarily within GPU and system memory without requiring excess local disk overhead. OVHcloud a100-720 is suited for large language model inference, distributed deep learning model training, high-performance computing simulations, and matrix-intensive data processing.
description: OVHcloud a100-720 is a GPU-accelerated virtual instance designed for compute-heavy parallel workloads. Provisioned via the KVM hypervisor on x86_64 architecture, it is configured with 60 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 3.0 GHz and 720 GB of system memory, yielding 12.0 GB per core. The server integrates four NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs totaling 320 GB of VRAM, with 80 GB per accelerator. Fast local scratch space is provided by a 500 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 25 Gbps network link. While the 500 GB local storage capacity requires supplementary cloud storage for oversized datasets, the resource balance makes the instance efficient for large model execution without paying for surplus local disk capacity. The a100-720 is tailored for distributed deep learning training, large language model inference, parallel scientific computing, and demanding matrix computation workloads.
